record.paper_title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity
record.context_brief: compact connected CDH spaces and SLH
record.original_question: Is every locally compact connected countable dense homogeneous space strongly locally homogeneous, and more generally is every compact connected countable dense homogeneous space strongly locally homogeneous?

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Is every (locally) compact connected CDH-space SLH?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological space $X$ is called *countable dense homogeneous* (CDH) if for any two countable dense subsets $D_1, D_2 \subseteq X$ there exists a homeomorphism $h: X \to X$ with $h(D_1) = D_2$. The space $X$ is called *strongly locally homogeneous* (SLH) if it has a base $\mathcal{B}$ of open sets such that for every $B \in \mathcal{B}$ and any two points $x, y \in B$, there exists a homeomorphism $h: X \to X$ with $h(x) = y$ and $h$ equal to the identity outside $B$.

Questions:
(a) Is every locally compact, connected, countable dense homogeneous space strongly locally homogeneous?
(b) More generally, is every compact, connected, countable dense homogeneous space strongly locally homogeneous?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on countable dense homogeneity (surveys and papers from 2014 onward, and works as recent as 2025) continues to discuss the relationship between CDH and SLH for compact/connected spaces. While partial results are known (e.g., every compact CDH space is strongly CDH; certain 2-homogeneous continua are SLH), no source identified resolves whether every (locally) compact connected CDH space must be SLH. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneity and topological groups
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work on CDH still references SLH vs CDH relationships without resolving the compact connected case.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the compact connected CDH implies SLH problem is reported in recent literature.
